Question: Let \(N\) be a positive multiple of \(5.\) One red ball and \(N\) green balls are arranged in a line in random order. Let \(P(N)\) be the probability that at least \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of the green balls are on the same side of the red ball. Observe that \(P(5)=1\) and that \(P(N)\) approaches \(\dfrac{4}{5}\) as \(N\) grows large. What is the sum of the digits of the least value of \(N\) such that \(P(N)\lt\dfrac{321}{400}?\)
